findings.title: Pass the chosen base to every base-sensitive check
findings.body: With `--base-ref refs/remotes/origin/main`, I confirmed that the generated plan reports `origin/main` but still passes `origin/dev` to `shared_git_surface_gate.py`. In a main-only clone, that preflight can fail before any suite runs. The release and frozen-case checks also consume `CCL_SKILL_BASE_REF`. Bind those checks to the selected candidate while preserving the clean environment needed by the Makefile-default regression.

findings.title: Apply Git isolation to executed commands as well as discovery
findings.body: A hook can invoke the selector with `GIT_INDEX_FILE` pointing into another checkout. Cleaning only discovery produces the right plan, but `_run_cmd()` still passes that index to preflights, parallel suites, and fallback Make targets. A selected shell suite that stages fixture files can then overwrite the caller’s index. Test a child launched through the execution path with a disposable caller index and verify its contents afterward.

findings.title: Remove Git overrides that can alter the commit graph
findings.body: The stated list omits `GIT_SHALLOW_FILE`, `GIT_GRAFT_FILE`, and `GIT_REPLACE_REF_BASE`, all recognized by the repository’s shared Git gate. For example, an inherited shallow file can make the feature tip appear parentless, causing base resolution to fail in a checkout with complete history. Tests using only `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_INDEX_FILE` would pass with this defect.

findings.title: Disable inherited hooks and templates in writable Git fixtures
findings.body: `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` still permits a system `core.hooksPath` and an inherited `GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR`. The latter can install an executable hook during fixture `git init`, and the fixture’s subsequent `git commit` runs it with the developer’s permissions. Disable system configuration and inherited templates or hooks, and exercise an actual fixture commit with a harmless sentinel hook.

findings.title: Constrain automatically executed suites to the checkout
findings.body: A changed `hooks/test_local.sh` symlink can point outside the worktree. Both `sibling_suites()` and `add_suite()` follow it with `is_file()`, and the runner executes the target with Bash. `--files ../test_local.sh` provides another route outside the checkout. Require containment of the resolved suite path before adding it to any executable plan.

findings.title: Preserve the single-document JSON output contract
findings.body: Applying the unconditional footer to `--json` appends plain text after the JSON object. The existing CLI test calls `json.loads(proc.stdout)` and would fail with extra data. Scope the human-readable footer to execution output, or carry the advisory in a JSON field while keeping stdout parseable.

findings.title: Fail discovery when any required Git enumeration fails
findings.body: A valid base does not establish that the staged, unstaged, and untracked queries succeeded. For example, a corrupt index can leave merge-base resolution working while `git diff --cached` fails. `collect_changed_files()` currently turns that failure into `[]`. A test that fails only a base-resolution command misses the resulting successful, incomplete plan.

findings.title: Reject unresolved or option-shaped explicit bases
findings.body: The missing-ref skip must apply only to automatic candidates. A typo in `CCL_SKILL_BASE_REF` can otherwise silently select a different target. I also confirmed that `--base-ref=--independent` is accepted as a `git merge-base` option and produces an empty plan. Resolve an explicit value to a commit with option parsing terminated before using it.

findings.title: Distinguish unrelated history from a failed base probe
findings.body: A clone can have a usable `origin/main` and an `origin/dev` with unrelated or shallow history. Both refs exist, but `git merge-base` returns 1 for the latter because it found no common ancestor. Treating every nonzero result on an existing automatic candidate as fatal rejects the usable main base.

findings.title: Preserve the configured default base for non-origin remotes
findings.body: A checkout using `CCL_SKILL_DEFAULT_BASE_REF=refs/remotes/upstream/dev` can resolve that base with the current selector. The proposed precedence drops it and exits 2 if the two hard-coded `origin` refs are absent, although the Makefile still accepts the setting. Define how a caller-supplied default reaches discovery and test an upstream-only checkout.

findings.title: Verify that `--repo` names the worktree root
findings.body: `git -C` searches parent directories even with routing variables removed. I confirmed that `--repo specs/test-affected --json` discovers the enclosing checkout’s changed files, while the planner looks for suites and scripts relative to `specs/test-affected`. Reject the mismatched root or consistently use Git’s resolved worktree root.

findings.title: Preserve exact filenames after NUL-delimited discovery
findings.body: `normalize_relpath()` still strips whitespace and changes literal backslashes into separators, including on the second normalization in `build_test_plan()`. A POSIX file named `hooks/test_a\b.py` can therefore select a different path after successful NUL-delimited parsing. An ordinary interior space and a UTF-8 name do not exercise this case or a filename containing undecodable bytes.

findings.title: Keep the slow abort-leak probe out of automatic self-selection
findings.body: For a change to `test_review_gate_abort_leak.sh`, I confirmed that the default plan lists the probe in both `parallel_suites` and `skipped_lanes`. The proposed self-run rule therefore executes an explicitly skipped probe alongside other suites, contrary to its dedicated-runner requirement. Test both the default skip and the serial slow run.

findings.title: Dispatch self-selected suites through their actual test runner
findings.body: The parallel runner invokes every `.py` suite as `python3 file.py`. A new pytest module containing a failing test but no main block exits zero without collecting the test. The sibling and self-selection checks can still pass because they inspect the selected filename. Exercise a deliberately failing pytest-style suite through the normal execution path.

findings.title: Define which exit code the parallel runner can preserve
findings.body: If a selected suite exits 7, `run-parallel-suites.sh` records 7 but returns 1 for any suite failure. GNU Make then returns 2 for the failed recipe. A test using only a serial child can verify exact propagation while the advertised `make test-affected` entry point returns a different status. Specify the contract at each boundary and test the real parallel path.

findings.title: Handle launch failures and signal exits in the terminal result
findings.body: If a selected executable such as `ruby` is missing, `subprocess.run()` raises `FileNotFoundError` before the selector can print its advisory. A directly signalled child instead returns a negative Python return code, which `sys.exit()` wraps into a different shell status. Neither case is covered by a child that simply calls `exit(7)`.

findings.title: Preserve the preflight phase in the execution contract
findings.body: The proposed sequence starts with parallel suites, but the current executor first runs `preflight_commands`, including the shared Git surface gate. An implementation following the stated sequence could still print those commands in dry-run output and pass the listed child-failure test while never executing them. Verify that a failing preflight prevents both parallel and serial work.

findings.title: Escape filename-bearing dry-run comments as well as command arguments
findings.body: The preview prints each changed filename after a single `#` prefix. A legal filename containing a newline can put an uncommented second line into the preview, which a shell will execute if the preview is replayed. Shell-quoting only the command arguments leaves this path open. Test the entire rendered preview with a multiline filename.

findings.title: Retain missing Makefile registrations until drift is checked
findings.body: If a newly registered hook suite is later removed from disk while its Makefile recipe remains, `makefile_suites()` filters it out before the planner can report drift. The literal-path unit test cannot see a registration that exists only in the Makefile. Exercise the fallback by leaving a missing hook suite registered and selecting an unmapped hook change.

findings.title: Include runtime skips in the promised skip summary
findings.body: With `FULL=1`, the Docker executable installed, and its daemon stopped, the selector schedules the sandbox suite. The suite prints `SKIP` and exits zero, so the planner’s `skipped_lanes` remains empty. The final summary can omit the very slow lane that did not run. Test this separately from a lane skipped during planning.

findings.title: State which focused checks still require local execution
findings.body: A change to `scripts/verify-sandbox/` requires `make test-verify-sandbox` under its directory contract. Neither root `make test` nor the CI workflow runs that target. A contributor following the footer and relying on the claim that CI runs every lane can land the change without exercising the sandbox. The root contract also requires affected focused tests and additional local checks for shared skill text.
